Whose water, whose power, whose backyard? Inside the real cost of the $650 billion AI buildout--and the fight against it. | | and | Jun 1 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- by Lawrence Winnerman The word we were given was cloud. It is one of the most effective pieces of marketing in the history of technology, because it tells you the thing is weightless, floating, somewhere up there and nowhere in particular--a place your photos live, made of nothing, costing nothing, sitting on no one. Ask Beverly and Jeff Morris what the cloud weighs. They live in Newton County, Georgia, in the kind of rural country people from the cities drive through without seeing. In 2018, Meta broke ground on a data center about a thousand feet from their home. Within months, the Morrises' well--the private well their household actually drinks from --began to fail. Sediment in the water. The dishwasher, the ice maker, the washing machine, the toilet, all faltering. They have spent roughly $5,000 trying to fix it and can't afford the $25,000 it would take to replace the well. Meta commissioned a study and concluded its data center was "unlikely" to have affected their groundwater. Three of the Morrises' neighbors have reported well trouble since the data center went in. The cloud, it turns out, has to land somewhere. It landed on them. This is an essay about where the cloud actually touches the ground--and about the fact that the people it's landing on hardest are not the people you'd expect, not the laid-off coders in the blue cities, but the farmers and retirees and well-water families in rural America who never signed up to host the most resource-hungry machine ever built. It is also an essay about the most interesting political possibility I've seen in years, which is what happens when those two groups of people figure out they're fighting the same thing. The Thing the Recession Is Hiding Inside I wrote, , that the AI buildout is the only thing currently propping up the American economy--that strip out the estimated $650 billion in data-center capital spending and the non-AI economy is flat on its back. That's the macro picture: the buildout is the cushion hiding the recession. Here's what that abstraction looks like when it lands in a county. The "buildout" is not a number on a balance sheet to the people who live next to it. It is a building the size of a small town, running twenty-four hours a day, sold to their county commission as jobs and tax base and the future. What arrives instead is a windowless industrial complex that employs a few dozen people once construction ends, draws the electricity of a city, drinks from the same water table the farms and the wells draw from, and never sleeps. The recession is hiding inside the buildout. And the buildout is hiding inside their backyard. Sponsored by Ground News A quick word on how to read a story this big. You are going to see this data-center fight told in completely different ways depending on where you get your news. The O'Leary project (below) alone gets framed as a patriotic national-security win on one outlet, an ecological catastrophe on the next, and a "Chinese influence operation" on a third--same project, three different realities, depending on which feed you happen to live in. The tool we use to see all of it at once is Ground News. They pull a single story together from across 50,000+ outlets and lay the bias breakdown out on a bar--left, center, right--so you can see who's covering it, who's spinning it, and who's quietly ignoring it. Their factuality ratings flag which sources actually check their work. On a story this contested, reading it through one outlet is how you get played. See every angle and get 40% off unlimited access: . Water Start with water, because water is where this gets visceral, and because it's where Erin Brockovich-- planted her flag. Data centers run hot. The machines inside them throw off enormous heat, and a great deal of that heat is managed with water--evaporative cooling that consumes the water rather than returning it. A large facility can draw up to 5 million gallons a day, the daily water use of a town of tens of thousands of people, and as much as 85 percent of it evaporates and never comes back to the local supply. In 2023, U.S. data centers consumed an estimated 17.4 billion gallons of water; the EPA projects that figure could reach 38 to 73 billion gallons by 2028. In a wet year, in a place with water to spare, you might never notice. But these facilities are not only being built in wet places, and the years are not reliably wet anymore. Then there is the version of the story where the rules simply don't apply to you. Twenty miles south of Atlanta, in Fayette County, a data-center campus developed by Quality Technology Services--owned by the private-equity giant Blackstone--drew roughly 29 million gallons of water through two connections the county utility didn't even know existed. One pipe had been installed without the utility's knowledge; the other was never tied into the billing system. The unmetered draw ran for about 15 months, and came to light only when residents started complaining about low water pressure at their own taps--some of them having been told, at the time, to stop watering their lawns. It became public when a local attorney, James Clifton, obtained the utility's letter to the company through a public-records request. The company owed about $147,000 in retroactive charges. The county declined to levy any fine. The explanation from the county water-system director, Vanessa Tigert, when asked why not, is the single most clarifying sentence in this entire essay: "They're our largest customer, and we have to be partners. It's called customer service." There it is, in one official's words: the public's water, taken outside the rules, at a scale no household could ever match, and the regulator's instinct is not to enforce the law but to apologize to the violator for the inconvenience of being noticed. The pattern repeats wherever this lands. A facility consumes a public resource at industrial scale, the rules that are supposed to govern that consumption turn out to be soft or unenforced, and the cost--the dropped water table, the fouled well, the dry season made drier--is socialized onto the people who live there while the benefit is captured a thousand miles away. This is the shape of story Erin Brockovich built a career on: a community, a stolen or poisoned water supply, a powerful entity that assumed no one in a small place would fight back. And she has now turned directly to data centers. In the spring of 2026 she launched a public reporting map, asking residents to self-report data-center problems in their own communities--and drew nearly 4,000 submissions in the first month. The single most common complaint, she reported, wasn't noise or water or the utility bill. It was one word that kept appearing in submission after submission: transparency. Nobody asked these communities first. | | ---|---|--- Heat Here is the cost almost no one names, because it is the most counterintuitive of all: the heat itself, and the water that is gone for good. Follow the water one step further than we did a moment ago. When a data center cools itself by evaporation, that water is not borrowed and returned a little dirtier, the way it is when you run a tap. It is consumed. Up to 85 percent of it rises into the sky as vapor and does not come back to that aquifer, that river, that town--not this season, maybe not ever. The water it does eventually discharge is often so loaded with the biocides and anti-corrosion chemicals used in the cooling loop that it's unfit to drink or to farm with. In a wet place you can pretend that's a wash. In a desert, it is a one-way withdrawal from an account that was already overdrawn. Then there is the heat, and the heat is pure physics. A data center does not make energy vanish; it converts it--essentially all of it--into heat. This is just the first law of thermodynamics: the electricity that pours into the building has to go somewhere, and where it goes, almost in its entirety, is back out as waste heat. A facility drawing a gigawatt of power is, functionally, a one-gigawatt furnace running in open country, around the clock, forever. Now look at what Kevin O'Leary is building. O'Leary--"Mr. Wonderful" from Shark Tank --is the public face of the Stratos Project, nicknamed "Wonder Valley," a data-center campus planned for some 40,000 acres of high desert in Box Elder County, Utah, just north of the already-shrinking Great Salt Lake. The buildout could run past $100 billion and is designed for around 9 gigawatts of power--more than double what the entire state of Utah uses in a year. A physics professor at Utah State University, Robert Davies, estimates that once you account for the inefficiency of the on-site natural-gas plant meant to power it, the real thermal load approaches 16 gigawatts--and that dumping that much heat into one valley could raise local nighttime temperatures by 8 to 12 degrees. Hold that number against the most infamous yardstick we have. By Davies's estimate, the heat this single campus would shed amounts to something on the order of 23 Hiroshima bombs' worth of energy--every day. I want to be precise, because the comparison is easy to abuse: this is total energy , released slowly as heat over twenty-four hours, not a blast in a single second over a city. Nobody is detonating anything. But the energy bookkeeping is real, and it is poured, hour after hour, into one fragile, water-starved place that never agreed to absorb it. This is the ecological cost that water and electricity figures alone miss. It isn't only that the machine drinks the water and bids up the power. It's that it takes the water permanently and bleeds a city's worth of heat into a small, dry, living place--near a dying lake and a migratory-bird sanctuary--on a timeline measured in decades. And the people who can see that most clearly are the ones who live there. In May 2026, hundreds of Box Elder County residents packed the fairgrounds chanting "Shame! Shame! Shame!" as commissioners voted the project through anyway; one of them, Brenna Williams, who is helping lead a referendum effort to overturn the approval, put it plainly: "We're already being told to ration our water." When O'Leary responded to the opposition by suggesting on Fox that his critics were "proxies for the Chinese government"--singling out two Utah political consultants, Gabi Finlayson and Jackie Morgan--Finlayson's reply wrote itself: "The only foreign operative here is a Canadian." Electricity Then there's the power, and this is the one that reaches even the households that never see a data center. These facilities consume staggering amounts of electricity, and that demand doesn't stay politely contained. It bids against you. A single large AI data center can require more than a gigawatt of power--as much as a major city, or a large nuclear plant--and when that demand hits the grid, the cost of supplying it lands on everyone's bill. The clearest place to see it is PJM, the grid operator that serves 13 states and the District of Columbia. In its 2025-2026 capacity auction, prices didn't tick up--they detonated, an 833 percent jump from the year before, from $28.92 to $269.92 per megawatt-day, the sharpest single-year increase in the market's history. Those costs flow straight through to consumers. The Natural Resources Defense Council found that data-center growth accounted for $9.3 billion of a $14 billion regional capacity bill, translating to roughly $70 a month for a typical household, and projected $100 billion to $163 billion in cumulative ratepayer costs through 2033 unless regulators intervene. In Washington, D.C., Pepco residential customers saw bills rise about $21 a month starting in mid-2025. Across the PJM region, supply rates have climbed between 5 and 44 percent since June of that year. So the family that has never heard the word "hyperscaler" still pays for it, in the line item on the utility bill that keeps climbing for reasons no one at the kitchen table can see. And the demand is so enormous, so fast, that it is bending the entire energy trajectory of the country backward. In the PJM region, utilities have delayed or canceled the retirement of roughly 60 percent of the fossil-fuel capacity that had been scheduled to shut down; at least 15 coal plants have had their closures pushed back since the start of 2025 alone, to feed rising demand. The cleaner energy future we'd been promised is being quietly deferred to run the machine. And in the single most vivid emblem of the moment, the Three Mile Island nuclear plant--site of the worst commercial nuclear accident in American history--is being brought back from the dead.No, really. Its Unit 1 reactor, retired in 2019 and now rebranded the Crane Clean Energy Center, is being restarted by Constellation Energy under a 20-year deal to sell its entire output to Microsoft, to power AI. The U.S. Department of Energy closed a $1 billion federal loan to help make it happen. It is on track to restart around 2027. O, brave new world! We are restarting Three Mile Island to run chatbots. If you wanted a single image for deploying a technology faster than we can think it through, you could not invent a better one than reopening the most infamous nuclear site in the country--with a billion dollars of public credit--to feed a machine whose business case is still, charitably, unproven. | | ---|---|--- Where It Lands, and on Whom Now the part that I think matters most, the part the national conversation keeps missing. We have been telling the story of AI and jobs as a blue-state, white-collar story: the laid-off marketing coordinator in Portland, the legal researcher in Cleveland, the coder in Austin. That story is real--. But it is only half the map. The other half is rural, much of it red, and for those communities the impact isn't an abstraction arriving in a quarterly earnings call. It is physical. Roughly two-thirds of new data centers are being built in rural areas, much of it on former farmland--developers have offered farmers as much as $120,000 an acre or more, several times the going rate, which sounds like a windfall until you realize it multiplies the price of the land around it and puts expansion permanently out of reach for the family farm next door. It is the constant low roar of cooling systems where there used to be quiet. It is the well, and the water table, and the electricity bill. It is the transformation of an exquisitely beautiful place into infrastructure, decided by a county commission dazzled by a tax-abatement deal, on behalf of a company headquartered in a city those residents will never visit. This is the rubber-meets-the-road moment of the AI economy, and it is happening in exactly the communities the coastal AI conversation has trained itself to ignore. The blue-city knowledge worker loses a job and feels the future as a closing door. The red-county farmer watches the future bulldoze the back forty and drain the well. Same machine. Same handful of companies. Same direction--pointed at extraction, with the gains captured far away and the costs left on the land. Different victims, who have been carefully taught to believe they are on opposite sides. They are not on opposite sides. That is the most important sentence in this essay. The Coalition Hiding in Plain Sight Here is the political possibility, and it is a big one. Across the country, rural communities are already organizing against data centers--forming groups, packing county-commission meetings, challenging zoning variances and tax abatements, demanding environmental review, and in a striking number of cases, winning. In Tucson, Arizona, residents raised enough alarm about water and energy that a proposed Amazon project was abandoned. In Saline Township, Michigan, residents voted down a $16 billion OpenAI-and-Oracle project. In Mason County, Kentucky, more than 1,500 residents have been turning out to plan opposition and pack hearings, and farmers there rejected a multimillion-dollar offer for their land. This is not happening because those communities read the same Substacks as the laid-off coder in Portland. It's happening because the cloud landed on them and they could see it. What makes this the most interesting development in American politics right now is that it is genuinely, structurally cross-partisan--and it's already being noticed. A March 2026 Gallup survey found that 71 percent of Americans oppose the construction of an AI data center in their own community, with nearly half strongly opposed--the first time Gallup had asked the question, and it arrived higher than opposition to a nuclear power plant has ever registered in the quarter-century Gallup has tracked it. Can you imagine? Americans would now rather live next to a nuclear reactor than a data center. In May 2026, even The New York Times ran a piece on liberals and conservatives finding common ground against the buildout. The fight does not care how you vote. The retiree in red Georgia whose well filled with sediment and the union organizer in a blue city worried about displacement are, whether either of them knows it yet, fighting the same concentration of power, in the same direction, for the same reason. The thing that has kept them apart is not their interests. It's the story they've each been told about the other. Erin Brockovich is a useful patron saint for exactly this reason. Her whole career has been small communities--not left communities or right communities, just communities --discovering that a powerful entity has quietly decided their water doesn't matter, and refusing to accept it. That is a politics older and deeper than the red-blue divide, and the data-center buildout is generating it at scale, in real time, in places the political class isn't watching. Sponsored by Ground News One more thing, because it 's the whole point of this piece. I argued above that the rural-red water fight and the blue-city labor fight are the same fight -- and that the thing keeping those people apart is the story each was told about the other. That's not an accident. It's what happens when your news comes from one side of the aisle and the other side's coverage is simply invisible to you. Ground News built a feature called Blindspot for exactly this: it surfaces the stories the left isn't covering and the stories the right isn't covering, side by side, so you can see what your own feed is hiding from you. The data-center buildout is a textbook case--covered hard by local and progressive outlets, underplayed by the national press that should be all over it. If you want to break out of the bubble that keeps this coalition from forming, start here: --40% off unlimited access. What to Do If you've read the other pieces in this series, you know I refuse to end on dread. So here is the turn to action, and for this fight it is unusually concrete, because the data-center buildout is one of the few pieces of this whole AI story that can actually be fought--and beaten--at the local level. You cannot personally slow the frontier labs. You can absolutely show up at a county-commission meeting. Find out what 's proposed near you. Data-center projects move through local zoning and permitting before they're built. That process is public, and it is where these fights are won or lost--on the tax abatement, the water permit, the environmental review, the zoning variance. The deal is usually struck before most residents have heard about it. Hearing about it early is half the battle. Connect to the people already fighting. Erin Brockovich has built a hub specifically for this: an interactive map of data centers across the country--operational, under construction, and proposed--overlaid with the locations where residents have reported problems, plus a form to report what's happening in your own community. If there's a project near you, you can find it; if there's a problem, you can put it on the map. Start there: . Build the coalition that scares them. The single most powerful thing about this fight is that it crosses the aisle. If you are a progressive reading this, the most useful thing you can do is show up for a rural community's water fight without making them pass a political purity test first. The concentration of power that drains their well is the same one coming for your livelihood. Act like it. | | ---|---|--- The Cloud Has to Land Somewhere There is no cloud. There was never a cloud. There is a machine, and the machine is made of concrete and copper and water and an appetite for electricity that is reshaping the physical landscape of the country, and it has to be built somewhere, and "somewhere" is turning out to be the quiet, beautiful, underdefended places where people assumed no one important was paying attention. The companies building it are counting on the same thing every powerful entity in a Brockovich story has ever counted on: that the place is too small, too rural, too scattered, too far from the cameras to fight back. And they are counting on one more thing--that the laid-off worker in the blue city and the dried-out farmer in the red county will never look up from their separate griefs long enough to notice they are being ground down to dust by the same machine. The cloud has to land somewhere. It's landing on us. All of us. Time to find each other. Sources The Morris family, Newton County, Georgia. Meta data center, construction begun 2018; well failure, sediment, roughly $5,000 spent and $25,000 to replace, Meta's "unlikely" finding, neighbors' reported well trouble. The New York Times , 2025, and corroborating coverage. Data-center water use. Up to ~5 million gallons/day for a large facility; up to ~85 percent evaporative loss; ~17.4 billion gallons consumed by U.S. data centers in 2023; EPA projection of 38-73 billion gallons by 2028. Environmental and Energy Study Institute (EESI); U.S. EPA. Fayette County, Georgia (the "customer service" case). Quality Technology Services (QTS), a Blackstone company; 615-acre Fayetteville campus; roughly 29 million gallons drawn through two connections over ~15 months; about $147,474 in retroactive charges; no fine levied. Brought to light by attorney James Clifton via public-records request; quote from county water-system director Vanessa Tigert. Tom 's Hardware, The Daily Caller , Cybernews, and POLITICO/E&E coverage, May 2026. Erin Brockovich data-center campaign. Public reporting map at brockovichdatacenter.com, launched spring 2026; nearly 4,000 community submissions in the first month; "transparency" cited as the most common concern. The Brockovich Report ; Newsweek ; TechCrunch , 2026. The Stratos Project / "Wonder Valley" (Kevin O'Leary), Box Elder County, Utah. ~9-gigawatt AI data center plus on-site natural-gas plant; ~40,000-acre campus near the Great Salt Lake; potential buildout cost exceeding $100 billion; "more than double" the electricity Utah uses in a year; approved by the Box Elder County Commission, May 4, 2026, amid protest; referendum effort underway. CNN (Clare Duffy, May 9, 2026); Salt Lake Tribune ; Fortune ; Common Dreams. Utah State University physicist Robert Davies : real thermal load approaching ~16 GW accounting for gas-plant inefficiency; projected local nighttime temperature rise of 8-12°F; the "~23 atomic bombs of heat per day" framing (reported via ZME Science and corroborating coverage). Resident Brenna Williams ("ration our water") via Common Dreams. O'Leary's "proxies for the Chinese government" remark and the Gabi Finlayson / Jackie Morgan "only foreign operative here is a Canadian" reply via Business Insider , HuffPost , and Yahoo. Waste-heat math (for the "Hiroshima" comparison). A data center converts essentially all input electricity to heat (first law of thermodynamics). Using Davies's effective ~16 GW figure: 16 GW × 86,400 seconds ≈ 1.38 × 1015 joules/day. Hiroshima ("Little Boy") ≈ 15 kilotons TNT ≈ 6.28 × 1013 joules. 1.38 × 1015 ÷ 6.28 × 1013 ≈ 22 Hiroshima-equivalents of energy per day, consistent with the "~23 bombs/day" figure in circulation. Comparison is of total energy released slowly as heat, not destructive blast delivered instantaneously. At the nameplate 9 GW the figure would be ~12/day; the higher number reflects the physicist's full-system estimate and is attributed to him in text. Electricity / PJM. 2025-2026 capacity auction rose from $28.92 to $269.92 per megawatt-day (~833 percent), the largest single-year increase in PJM history. Utility Dive ; DataCenterDynamics. NRDC: data-center growth responsible for $9.3 billion of a $14 billion PJM capacity bill, ~$70/month for a typical household, $100-163 billion cumulative ratepayer costs projected through 2033. Natural Resources Defense Council; Citizens Utility Board, 2025. Pepco residential bills up ~$21/month in Washington, D.C., from mid-2025; PJM-region supply rates up 5-44 percent since June 2025. E&E News/POLITICO. Coal retirements / Three Mile Island. Roughly 60 percent of scheduled PJM fossil-fuel retirements delayed or canceled; 15+ coal plants pushed back since January 2025. OilPrice.com ; EnergyNow. Three Mile Island Unit 1 (retired 2019), rebranded Crane Clean Energy Center; Constellation Energy 20-year PPA with Microsoft; $1 billion DOE loan closed November 2025; targeted restart ~2027. Constellation Energy; Orrick; NucNet. Rural siting and farmland. Roughly two-thirds of new data centers built in rural areas, much on former farmland; offers up to ~$120,000/acre and higher. Brookings Institution; Farm Progress. Local outcomes. Tucson, Arizona (Amazon project abandoned); Saline Township, Michigan ($16 billion OpenAI-Oracle project voted down); Mason County, Kentucky (1,500+ residents organizing; farmers rejected a multimillion-dollar offer). Brookings Institution; Civil Eats ; The New York Times. Public opinion. Gallup, "Americans Oppose AI Data Centers in Their Area," released May 13, 2026 (telephone survey by Recon MR, March 2-18, 2026, n=1,000): 71 percent oppose a local AI data center (48 percent strongly); opposition exceeds the highest level Gallup has recorded for nuclear power plants since it began asking in 2001. "Man, you called AI before anyone else." I get a version of that just about every day.
The sentiment is nice, but there were several people who were jumping up and down about automation and jobs even before I was. One of them is technologist Martin Ford, whom I interview on the podcast this week.
"People are arguing right now about whether we are seeing AI replace workers," Martin observes. "My point is that, even if it's not happening now, it will be happening eventually. With the development of both AI and robotics, it's inevitable that the bulk of human workers will eventually be replaced. And some data shows that it's happening now with entry-level jobs, particularly in computer programming and customer service roles."
Martin wrote the seminal book, "Rise of the Robots: Technology and the Threat of a Jobless Future" way back in 2015. He had an earlier book, "Lights in the Tunnel" that made a similar case way back in 2009. I was profoundly influenced by Martin and read both books before I ran for President. What can I say? I read a lot. Martin argues for Universal Basic Income in Rise of the Robots. "In my view, the most effective solution is likely to be some form of basic income guarantee." He describes a vision of a consumer market as a renewable resource with people receiving money that they then turn around and spend.
Right now though, Martin fears that the current changes are going to get rocky indeed. "Many of the workers whom I believe may be most subject to replacement by AI are highly-paid white-collar workers, like accountants and lawyers. As they lose their salaries, it's going to hurt their ability to pay their mortgages or consume. The top 10% of earners account for 50% of spending in the consumer economy, and even if a basic income were to be implemented it wouldn't be enough to make up for the loss of buying power."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/16254481-bbd4-4cca-8f1d-463a2ac03645?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Martin also observes that labor replacement isn't linear, but tends to spike in a downturn. "History shows that automation technologies get rolled out most actively in a recession, and there's a chance we might be heading toward one now." For example, 13% of credit card accounts are now delinquent, the highest rate in over a decade.
Martin also thinks that the current spending assumes substantial labor replacement. Here's the math: $725 billion will be spent on AI data centers and infrastructure this year. How could corporate America spend $725 billion and not expect some of it to come back via reduced labor costs? I just came back from Michigan where they are trying to clear the way for more data centers in their state because the centers bring with them significant ongoing tax revenue. Martin says, "One argument is that it will increase productivity and enable big companies to do more. But with that much invested, reducing labor costs will be the low-hanging fruit."
AI is in the news this week as several major companies have seen shaky returns from their early spending; one major company spent $500 million on AI tokens to little return, and is now reducing its spend. Other companies are reporting similar experiences. Simultaneously, Anthropic, OpenAI and others are gearing up for the biggest IPOs in history. You can almost sense them trying to reach the public markets so that they can realize hundreds of billions of dollars worth of liquidity before their ability to reach their lofty revenue projections gets called into question. It's a footrace on which the entire stock market depends, as a lot of the recent growth has been fueled by belief in AI. "I think the valuations are too high based on what these businesses are bringing in for revenue," Martin comments. But his concerns about labor replacement are bigger than any current valuation cycle. "This has been building up for years."
Martin is nothing if not consistent - I saw him at TED in 2017. "I used to talk about this and people would see it as an interesting topic for the future, maybe twenty years out. Now, they think it's very relevant to the present day. I see my job as trying to get smart people talking about this so we can address some of these issues." He's not the only one.
For my conversation with Martin Ford, the author of "[Rise of the Robots: Technology and the Threat of a Jobless Future](https://substack.com/redirect/a3f1e8cf-1995-4dc4-85db-b5f79d7dff45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" click [here](https://substack.com/redirect/e0fee14d-7813-4618-b438-389e7ad2e015?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). One of them is technologist Martin Ford, whom I interview on the podcast this week. "People are arguing right now about whether we are seeing AI replace workers," Martin observes. "My point is that, even if it's not happening now, it will be happening eventually. With the development of both AI and robotics, it's inevitable that the bulk of human workers will eventually be replaced. And some data shows that it's happening now with entry-level jobs, particularly in computer programming and customer service roles." Martin wrote the seminal book, "Rise of the Robots: Technology and the Threat of a Jobless Future" way back in 2015. He had an earlier book, "Lights in the Tunnel" that made a similar case way back in 2009. I was profoundly influenced by Martin and read both books before I ran for President. What can I say? I read a lot. Martin argues for Universal Basic Income in Rise of the Robots. "In my view, the most effective solution is likely to be some form of basic income guarantee." He describes a vision of a consumer market as a renewable resource with people receiving money that they then turn around and spend. Right now though, Martin fears that the current changes are going to get rocky indeed. "Many of the workers whom I believe may be most subject to replacement by AI are highly-paid white-collar workers, like accountants and lawyers. As they lose their salaries, it's going to hurt their ability to pay their mortgages or consume. The top 10% of earners account for 50% of spending in the consumer economy, and even if a basic income were to be implemented it wouldn't be enough to make up for the loss of buying power." | | ---|---|--- Martin also observes that labor replacement isn't linear, but tends to spike in a downturn. "History shows that automation technologies get rolled out most actively in a recession, and there's a chance we might be heading toward one now." For example, 13% of credit card accounts are now delinquent, the highest rate in over a decade. Martin also thinks that the current spending assumes substantial labor replacement. Here's the math: $725 billion will be spent on AI data centers and infrastructure this year. How could corporate America spend $725 billion and not expect some of it to come back via reduced labor costs? I just came back from Michigan where they are trying to clear the way for more data centers in their state because the centers bring with them significant ongoing tax revenue. Martin says, "One argument is that it will increase productivity and enable big companies to do more. But with that much invested, reducing labor costs will be the low-hanging fruit." AI is in the news this week as several major companies have seen shaky returns from their early spending; one major company spent $500 million on AI tokens to little return, and is now reducing its spend. Other companies are reporting similar experiences. Simultaneously, Anthropic, OpenAI and others are gearing up for the biggest IPOs in history. You can almost sense them trying to reach the public markets so that they can realize hundreds of billions of dollars worth of liquidity before their ability to reach their lofty revenue projections gets called into question. It's a footrace on which the entire stock market depends, as a lot of the recent growth has been fueled by belief in AI. "I think the valuations are too high based on what these businesses are bringing in for revenue," Martin comments. But his concerns about labor replacement are bigger than any current valuation cycle. "This has been building up for years." Martin is nothing if not consistent - I saw him at TED in 2017. "I used to talk about this and people would see it as an interesting topic for the future, maybe twenty years out. Now, they think it's very relevant to the present day. I see my job as trying to get smart people talking about this so we can address some of these issues." He's not the only one. For my conversation with Martin Ford, the author of "" click . May was a tremendous month of growth for Team Marialana Kinter. Together, our volunteers knocked on more than 2,000 doors across Congressional District 7, helping us connect directly with voters and build momentum for the campaign. We were also excited to welcome Lee Perry as our new Campaign Manager as we continue expanding our grassroots operation. Looking ahead, we are building a stronger coalition canvassing program that will bring together candidates up and down the ballot throughout Seminole and Volusia counties.
By sharing volunteers, resources, and organizing efforts, we can help more candidates reach voters before the August 18 election and strengthen our movement for accountable leadership. Thank you to everyone who knocked doors, tabled at events, made phone calls, and helped spread our message. Please encourage your friends and family to make a voting plan through their county Supervisor of Elections website and join our movement to talk with voters, fight corruption, and help bring real change to our communities. Every conversation matters, and we cannot do this without you.

Whether you have just a few hours a week or can go all-in, every single volunteer makes a huge impact.
Here’s how you can help:

* Phone banking & texting voters
* Door knocking in your neighborhood
* Social media amplification
* Data entry & campaign operations
* Yard sign distribution
* And more!

**Ready to get involved?**

Friend, we only have one more day until New Mexico’s primary election—and I’m up against a Democratic opponent funded by many of the same donors who helped elect Donald Trump. **[Will you rush $5 right now to help us win this race and keep New Mexico moving forward?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/9552?t=3&akid=9977%2E400544%2EJQTIXo) ** _However, if you’d like to know more about why your donation today is so essential, let me share why I’m running for Governor and what’s at stake in this election._

I come from generations of resilient and fierce Pueblo women.

It's thanks to these women — like my mom, who served in the U.S. Navy, raised four kids as a military wife, and then devoted 25 years to Indian education at the Bureau of Indian Affairs — that I summoned the courage to run for office.

It led me to become one of the first Native American women elected to Congress and, later on, the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history!
History has shown us that there's nothing we can't accomplish if we work together. **No state in America has ever elected a Native American woman as Governor — but with your support, I know we can change that.**

**So please, friend, ahead of tomorrow’s primary election, I have to ask:[_Will you chip in $5 or more right now to help me become the first Native American woman elected Governor and keep New Mexico blue?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/9552?t=5&akid=9977%2E400544%2EJQTIXo)**

body:
A court just ruled that corporations have the legal right to vote in American elections.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001VMiz4yBfFEPt7mkZy0WHm7r0zdOPuKInjv-8QHc5dD4C-S8A3w3cyHdJL_RuN_5lECMDwBwgfScLGRK1HdAvBQL6DPmeY9DsrDeCpmSSrDXAv9VmKXTnfhFHVHq5simeFa4IXbN0F4zGmqaCifOb3beerN-FKnXnNW96Dva-HLikGRBofL7Jj_tfiPp3O1Lwm7VN9m9NWh7cuxXKpYWTQVemV06cGK5bljI49IvGTTM=&c=bzf7t0mFQu6KLlflvMsbPg1tqOjyw6n7AzEe0bJLVcWPzfmFcwc6ig==&ch=XT_ahHxAhVEehbBwmfKFtw185MjN5qH2eFEyPS4SX_NGvn26EoexCw==)

|
Peter,
A judge in Delaware just laid the foundation for Citizens United Part 2. And this sequel will definitely be worse than the original.
Citizens United vs. FEC was the landmark decision that broke our politics by opening the door to unlimited political spending. In its decision, SCOTUS ruled that corporations had a right to free speech, and equated speech to money. In the decade and a half since, elected officials and candidates have been forced to focus on appeasing billionaire funded superPACs instead of their constituents.
Citizens United made it possible for billionaire and corporate dark money networks to capture our government and the judiciary at every level. But this latest decision somehow has the potential to be even more catastrophic for democracy:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001VMiz4yBfFEPt7mkZy0WHm7r0zdOPuKInjv-8QHc5dD4C-S8A3w3cyHdJL_RuN_5lECMDwBwgfScLGRK1HdAvBQL6DPmeY9DsrDeCpmSSrDXAv9VmKXTnfhFHVHq5simeFa4IXbN0F4zGmqaCifOb3beerN-FKnXnNW96Dva-HLikGRBofL7Jj_tfiPp3O1Lwm7VN9m9NWh7cuxXKpYWTQbz6MreRfnTX8TSRJEngF40=&c=bzf7t0mFQu6KLlflvMsbPg1tqOjyw6n7AzEe0bJLVcWPzfmFcwc6ig==&ch=XT_ahHxAhVEehbBwmfKFtw185MjN5qH2eFEyPS4SX_NGvn26EoexCw==)
---
A court just ruled that corporations have the legal right to vote in American elections. Not to spend money. Not to donate. To vote. And the Supreme Court MAGA extremist Leonard Leo built with $1.6 billion in dark money will decide whether it spreads to every election in the country.
MAGA cannot win fair elections. Trump's approval is at historic lows, Republican congressional disapproval has hit 86%, and voters are furious. So they are changing the rules. They gutted the Voting Rights Act, seized voter records in eight states, voided primary results after ballots were already cast, and built a $1.8 billion slush fund to pay the January 6th insurrectionists they need when they declare the midterms rigged.
Every step is designed to ensure that what voters want no longer determines who holds power. And the Supreme Court is the institution making all of it legal.
In 2020, state Supreme Courts were the firewall that kept the election results intact. We have been rebuilding that firewall ever since. We won in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin. Nevada, Kentucky, Montana, Michigan, and Minnesota are next, and every one of them will be targeted by the same dark money machine running this entire operation.
And while we hold that line, Unpack Our Courts is building the movement to reform and rebalance the Supreme Court itself. If the state firewall fails, there is no backstop. If the court is not reformed before Trump places two or three more justices, the fascist takeover they are plotting becomes a reality.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c-K2zAQBvCnkW82o79JDj4UvIFCd0vJoUejSGN7QJaEJG_p25csyQv0Oh98w2_m9_v8bilQXD_sjiPVOpc6tw3XgrbZHQs5G2tL5e8sQJgeTA98ziXVjK7NvPOjFvy8nDsc-ekMUnB90d02KpAGuDlrZcxFKwFC3aXnHLgS1t-XjsZHIRjgXCoNejCI-uLALvwu9XJyTMGRvW04UKzksbqUck6BGrk6pLJ2Ydxay5XJb0xcmbhSXNKwUQjV24AD-oOJ61IQ-y9O__L0X6Def3omr9UxOQGok_wAocQPrqef09vbjQlztH2u6SgOmZxeZorrM9rR07EzOeFuKTyHzu7Z0hqZnIKNPi1byjg_Vj3zFBvGxuT069R_v9361xW6Mvr8h0Kgak5MwfooHVzau_Y_f_kcxb8AAAD__79SnDc)

| |
Dear Friend of Liberty,

As we approach America's 250th anniversary, I have a question for you: **what story will the next generation learn about our country?**

You're an intelligent and civically engaged person. So, you know that right now, far too many colleges and universities teach young people a distorted view of America--as if our nation were built on injustice instead of liberty.

This false story robs college students--our future leaders--of a proper understanding of our American heritage and weakens the informed patriotism that preserves our freedom.

**But you can change that --and receive "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope," one of our most popular online courses, as a DVD box set--for FREE.**

Taught by historian Wilfred McClay and based on his published history of America, "**The Great American Story: A Land of Hope** " presents a full, unbiased account of America's past. It's a magnificent course, perfect for in-home viewing or with a small study group.

We produced this course to help restore intelligent patriotism, especially in young people, which is essential for the survival of free government.

**Will you take two simple steps right now?**

* First, claim your free copy of "The Great American Story" DVD box set to add to your home library. Simply tell us where to send it, and we'll ship it to your preferred address. There's no other obligation on your part!
* Second, after claiming your free DVD box set, consider helping place this course and other outreach efforts in homes nationwide by making a tax-deductible gift. That way, millions more Americans, especially young people, can learn the truth about our nation's history.

**But supplies are limited, so please act now using this secure link:
**
**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-great-american-story-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c-K2zAQBvCnkW82o79JDj4UvIFCd0vJoUejSGN7QJaEJG_p25csyQv0Oh98w2_m9_v8bilQXD_sjiPVOpc6tw3XgrbZHQs5G2tL5e8sQJgeTA98ziXVjK7NvPOjFvy8nDsc-ekMUnB90d02KpAGuDlrZcxFKwFC3aXnHLgS1t-XjsZHIRjgXCoNejCI-uLALvwu9XJyTMGRvW04UKzksbqUck6BGrk6pLJ2Ydxay5XJb0xcmbhSXNKwUQjV24AD-oOJ61IQ-y9O__L0X6Def3omr9UxOQGok_wAocQPrqef09vbjQlztH2u6SgOmZxeZorrM9rR07EzOeFuKTyHzu7Z0hqZnIKNPi1byjg_Vj3zFBvGxuT069R_v9361xW6Mvr8h0Kgak5MwfooHVzau_Y_f_kcxb8AAAD__79SnDc)**

If we don't teach the truth, young people will likely only hear lies--that America is an essentially unjust nation and unworthy of our love. We cannot let that happen, especially as America prepares to mark its 250th anniversary.

**You can make a difference.** With your gift today, you will help restore intelligent patriotism in the hearts of millions of Americans, just in time for the 250th celebration!

Thank you for helping others learn the truth about our history and America's great heritage of liberty. You are a true friend of freedom.

Warm regards,

Bill Gray, '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

# Mansharamani Musings
---
| | [](https://us.list-manage.com/_LoeIEewOtd?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)May was a month filled with some fascinating findings (see below for my piece on British Columbia). I had the opportunity to meet with government officials, business leaders, academics, journalists, and lots of young professionals. The worries over AI disruption continue to intensify, as you’ll see in the piece I published yesterday. Links to my other writings from May are below!
Best wishes for a thought-filled June!_**
- Vikram**_

---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZsqGN1mtxbK?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)
| | **May 3, 2026**

A few years ago, the United Nations adopted a framework called the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. It took over 25 years in international forums, far from the kitchen tables of British Columbia (BC), to be drafted. In 2019, however, the provincial legislature in Victoria unanimously [converted the global framework into binding BC law](https://us.list-manage.com/pe9tCYViojs?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586). Most legislators thought they were making a symbolic statement of good intent. Instead, they were threading a needle through the load-bearing seams of BC’s historical legal and economic order.
Last August, [after the longest trial in Canadian history](https://us.list-manage.com/im3nc7JRGjG?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), a BC Supreme Court judge declared that 3.25 square kilometers of Richmond (the fourth largest municipality in the province and home to almost a quarter million residents) sit atop land that is owned by the Cowichan Tribes. Specifically, the court found the homes, farms, and industrial sites on that land fall under Aboriginal title, deeming that historical and current grants of fee-simple ownership were defective. Stop and read that again. _The court ruled that those who live on the Cowichan land must now worry about whether they own the home they paid for and think they own_.,,

| | **May 10, 2026**

On April 17, the Japanese destroyer _Ikazuchi_ spent [14 hours transiting the Taiwan Strait](https://us.list-manage.com/yiSQTx2sMt_?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) with its tracking system turned off. China’s Eastern Theater Command scrambled naval and air forces to shadow it and released drone surveillance footage. Beijing called it [“a deliberate provocation”](https://us.list-manage.com/18ZrT2R25qq?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) and they weren’t entirely wrong.
April 17, 1895 is the date China signed the [Treaty of Shimonoseki](https://us.list-manage.com/YSNBm05ohgm?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), the “unequal” treaty that Japan de facto forced upon the Qing dynasty to cede Taiwan after losing [the First Sino-Japanese War](https://us.list-manage.com/QZb8DAlCige?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586). Taiwan was a Japanese colony for the next 50 years. For Beijing, it’s the original wound. And Japan just sailed a warship through it on the anniversary.
The _Ikazuchi_ transit wasn’t random. Last November, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told Japan’s parliament that a Chinese attack on Taiwan would produce an [“existential crisis for Japan”](https://us.list-manage.com/CvUqzPV8eoi?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) as the action would trigger a legal right to collective self-defense. The late Shinzo Abe, Takaichi’s mentor, [rewrote the legal framework](https://us.list-manage.com/_NYiSHk04Jk?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) in 2014 to enable such military action. It was the first time a sitting Japanese prime minister had ever cited Taiwan as a specific scenario for military action...

| | **May 17, 2026**

All of us understand that our world is increasingly interconnected, yet every day I stumble upon another example of the uncertainty magnifying impact of this reality. So how do drought in California, chocolate sales at the Dubai airport, an update to Starbucks’ menu, and the war in Iran connect to impact your life?
If you’ve bought pistachios lately, you’ve noticed that prices are up. In fact, prices hit an 8-year high ([$4.57 a pound in March](https://us.list-manage.com/gbvtYy66rwS?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)). Globally, pistachio prices are up [more than 50%](https://us.list-manage.com/C1yVOr8dKDc?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) in recent months. The most recent surge in price is the result of geopolitics, and the whole thing is, well, nuts.

I am referring, of course, to the war in Iran. The Islamic Republic is the world’s second-largest producer of pistachios, accounting for roughly [20 percent of global supply. ](https://us.list-manage.com/Yr4ZVR8pIoY?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)The country’s pistachios are prized for their rich flavor and have been desired for centuries in baklava, ice cream, and chocolate. Let’s not forget pistachios have also emerged as a top-seller in the snack aisle at your grocery store.

| | **May 24, 2026**

The South Korean stock market is booming. The KOSPI index is [up about 150% from its April 2025 low](https://us.list-manage.com/10UdxpitG2h?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) and gained ~75% percent in 2025. This is Korea’s best performance in over 25 years. But it hasn’t stopped this year. It’s already up more than 75% and recently touched the 8,000 level for the first time in history. For comparison, it was hovering around 2,500 two years ago.
Regular readers know I’ve had a lifelong interest in bubbles. Unsurprisingly, performance like this catches my attention. Six days after hitting 8,000, the KOSPI plunged around 12%, triggering downside circuit breakers. The very next day it [bounced 8%](https://us.list-manage.com/C2ybXKUm9s3?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) or so, triggering _an upside_ circuit breaker. It was starting to look less like a rally and more like a seizure. My bubble spotting seismograph was indicating tremors afoot...

| | **May 31, 2026**

It’s graduation season, and like Spring itself, it’s a time of renewal, hope, and new beginnings. It always brings back the excitement I felt decades ago, in the audience in cap and gown, my whole life ahead of me. It’s also the season of older people standing at podiums telling younger people what lies ahead and the secret sauce to living their lives. And it’s no easy task for the speaker: 15 minutes to make an impact on a crowd that’s hungover, sunburned, and already thinking about the after-party. They also already feel like they have all the answers – who doesn’t at that age?

Stated or not, there seems to be a simple rule for commencement speech success: energize the graduates and make them feel like they can take on the world...

On May 27, Kevin O'Leary went on NBC and called me out by name[ (check out 8:55 if you want to see the moment). ](https://substack.com/redirect/710b9921-b494-40b7-870d-bea090eb92a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
He told a national audience that I'm "putting out falsehoods," that I'm being funded by BEAR and Earthly Education propped up by Australian money, that Australia is "a vector for the Chinese," and that he has an "international team" digging into me. He mispronounced my name and couldn't say what party I belonged to. But he could stand on a national stage and suggest I'm a foreign operative. Here's my response:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/18c9fab5-07a6-4016-8267-4cf74fc2f8a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
First of all, My name is pronounced **Glyk** -- like "I like Gleich." Commit it to memory, Kevin, because you're going to be hearing a lot more from me.
Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..gd7HDNBRwSkmFd9WysGtOhXRfy8FYu_i2XOBx0SRGYI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=200026618)
The accusation is a lie, and it's projection.
Earthly Education has never paid me, funded me, or partnered with me in any capacity. I have not received a single dollar for any post I've made about this project. I've spent days of my own time on this, for free, because I live here and I love Utah.
He said in a social media post that [90% of the protesters are not people that live in Utah](https://substack.com/redirect/f2f71cf3-9129-4384-acd0-3d29655e5260?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), that they're being bussed in. Accusing someone of being paid or bussed in for protesting is the oldest trick in the book. If you can't discredit the message, then try to discredit the messengers. It's also peak DARVO (Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender).
His project has drawn international outrage and global attention. But global attention is not foreign funding. Those are not the same thing, and a man who built his brand on finance knows the difference.
Here's what makes the accusation rich. Kevin O'Leary is a citizen of Canada, Ireland, and the United Arab Emirates. He wrote on his own [LinkedIn](https://substack.com/redirect/710b9921-b494-40b7-870d-bea090eb92a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he believes "Abu Dhabi is going to become the capital of capital in the next 10 years" and that he wants "to be part of it." The American Conservative (not exactly a left-wing outlet) has [documented how the UAE hands citizenship to high-value foreigners](https://substack.com/redirect/466dfa7d-3cac-4789-8cbe-d884b432ad2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a strategic asset.
The only foreign dollars flowing into Utah around this data center are _his_. He is the foreign actor here, arriving under the banner of national security and accusing the locals of being the threat.
Every accusation is a confession.
The group O'Leary smeared on NBC is [BEAR](https://substack.com/redirect/37a07e25-2f3e-46d5-a61e-53317d4f735a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the Box Elder Accountability Referendum. BEAR is a grassroots group of local Utahn trying to hold their own county commissioners accountable through a ballot referendum.
O'Leary says he wants to win the trust of Box Elder County residents. He can start by not calling them Chinese sleeper cells on national television. That is not a man acting in good faith. That is a man making false statements with reckless disregard for the truth.
Here's what's actually not misinformation, Kevin:
Scientists at the University of Utah and Utah State, with their names attached, have [analyzed](https://substack.com/redirect/ecbe6675-b3be-4efe-9a4e-8adb3db0b2b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this project.[ Utah Clean Energy's analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/57f16423-a62c-4cab-94db-2caa02d67b19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) finds that at full 9-gigawatt build-out on combined-cycle gas turbines, the facility would emit roughly 30 million tons of CO2 a year. That would raise the entire state of Utah's carbon emissions by about 55%. The same analysis puts the water needed just to run the gas turbines at 16.6 billion gallons a year, enough to fill roughly 25,000 Olympic swimming pools.
The Great Salt Lake has lost the majority of its volume and [sits 6.5 feet below the minimum healthy level](https://substack.com/redirect/0664779b-ad87-4175-9730-915e2689ee21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The exposed lakebed is a[ toxic dust of heavy metals ](https://substack.com/redirect/d094cc1f-9c11-4caf-8b89-dd73a4d77619?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)threatening the air of two million Utahns downwind. The entire state is in a drought.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4011d402-cc22-4c02-a73f-f6c2c7ad4c9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

And when more than [3,800 Utahns each paid fifteen dollars ](https://substack.com/redirect/075f425e-b72a-4d31-ace0-9149f2b24b12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)to file formal protests against the project's water application, the developer pulled the application rather than face them.
The biggest issue is that this whole development was rammed through with zero public input and zero environmental impact studies. This project was fast-tracked through MIDA, which is Utah's Military Installation Development Authority. MIDA was created for a legitimate reason: to support development around Hill Air Force Base. MIDA has drifted a long way from defending an air base. It now functions as a vehicle that can hand a private developer enormous tax concessions and override the normal checks, with no daylight for the public. There was not a single meaningful opportunity for public input before this moved forward.
And consider how Utah law gets made. In the 2026 legislative session, lawmakers introduced [1,015 bills and passed 540 in 45 days](https://substack.com/redirect/08d4b477-36cd-4f09-aca9-f157c359f6c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The median bill gets only a few minutes of total debate across both chambers. [Senator Todd Weiler](https://substack.com/redirect/77402fcf-bafe-4c35-bafd-e790cb5856a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) said it plainly: "I know that the public wants every legislator to read and comprehend every bill, but in our 45-day session, it's not realistic." He even stood up, described a bill, and got it passed with no discussion, except he'd described the _wrong_ bill (it was later corrected).
Lobbyists likely fill that vacuum. According to [public records reviewed by Fox 13](https://substack.com/redirect/3c806ad0-8d10-46cf-984a-536ff3238905?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), O'Leary hired Lincoln-Hill Partners to lobby for this development. That firm has a long history with Utah politicians, including Senate President Stuart Adams, who sits on the MIDA board. The bills move faster than the public and lawmakers can read them. This process should bother every Utahns regardless of how they vote.
O'Leary says his international team is researching the protesters, spending money to investigate private citizens who showed up to exercise their first amendment rights and oppose his project. All because we keep asking questions, like what are these data centers actually going to be used for? Because computers at this scale, used for state surveillance and to monitor the people who protest, could become the infrastructure of exactly the thing he claims to be defending against. AI without guardrails, pointed at dissenters, isn't national defense. That's the authoritarian playbook. He is accusing us of being the threat while building the capacity to be one.
I'd love to make this case to the same national audience O'Leary used to smear me. As of now, NBC has not agreed to host me on broadcast for a rebuttal. So the accusation got the national stage and the correction did not.
The one thing Mr. Terrible has actually accomplished is uniting us. Republicans, Democrats, Independents, people who've never voted in their lives are coming together to defend Utah from a genuine foreign threat. O'Leary says he wants to support the people of Box Elder County. But the people who actually need funding here aren't billionaires with three passports. They're Utahns fighting to protect our air, our land, our water, and our future.
If you want to put money where it matters, chip in $5 or more to [BEAR](https://substack.com/redirect/37a07e25-2f3e-46d5-a61e-53317d4f735a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the residents of Box Elder exploring every option to hold their commissioners and their state legislature accountable. Or support my Substack here:
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..gd7HDNBRwSkmFd9WysGtOhXRfy8FYu_i2XOBx0SRGYI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=200026618)
That's where the real Utahns are. That's where your money should go.

He mispronounced my name and couldn't say what party I belonged to. But he could stand on a national stage and suggest I'm a foreign operative. Here's my response: First of all, My name is pronounced Glyk -- like "I like Gleich." Commit it to memory, Kevin, because you're going to be hearing a lot more from me. Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. The accusation is a lie, and it's projection. Earthly Education has never paid me, funded me, or partnered with me in any capacity. I have not received a single dollar for any post I've made about this project. I've spent days of my own time on this, for free, because I live here and I love Utah. He said in a social media post that , that they're being bussed in. Accusing someone of being paid or bussed in for protesting is the oldest trick in the book. If you can't discredit the message, then try to discredit the messengers. It's also peak DARVO (Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender). His project has drawn international outrage and global attention. But global attention is not foreign funding. Those are not the same thing, and a man who built his brand on finance knows the difference. Here's what makes the accusation rich. Kevin O'Leary is a citizen of Canada, Ireland, and the United Arab Emirates. He wrote on his own that he believes "Abu Dhabi is going to become the capital of capital in the next 10 years" and that he wants "to be part of it." The American Conservative (not exactly a left-wing outlet) has as a strategic asset. The only foreign dollars flowing into Utah around this data center are his. He is the foreign actor here, arriving under the banner of national security and accusing the locals of being the threat. Every accusation is a confession. The group O'Leary smeared on NBC is , the Box Elder Accountability Referendum. BEAR is a grassroots group of local Utahn trying to hold their own county commissioners accountable through a ballot referendum. O'Leary says he wants to win the trust of Box Elder County residents. He can start by not calling them Chinese sleeper cells on national television. That is not a man acting in good faith. That is a man making false statements with reckless disregard for the truth. Here's what's actually not misinformation, Kevin: Scientists at the University of Utah and Utah State, with their names attached, have this project. finds that at full 9-gigawatt build-out on combined-cycle gas turbines, the facility would emit roughly 30 million tons of CO2 a year. That would raise the entire state of Utah's carbon emissions by about 55%. The same analysis puts the water needed just to run the gas turbines at 16.6 billion gallons a year, enough to fill roughly 25,000 Olympic swimming pools. The Great Salt Lake has lost the majority of its volume and . The exposed lakebed is a the air of two million Utahns downwind. The entire state is in a drought. | | ---|---|--- And when more than file formal protests against the project's water application, the developer pulled the application rather than face them. The biggest issue is that this whole development was rammed through with zero public input and zero environmental impact studies. This project was fast-tracked through MIDA, which is Utah's Military Installation Development Authority. MIDA was created for a legitimate reason: to support development around Hill Air Force Base. MIDA has drifted a long way from defending an air base. It now functions as a vehicle that can hand a private developer enormous tax concessions and override the normal checks, with no daylight for the public. There was not a single meaningful opportunity for public input before this moved forward. And consider how Utah law gets made. In the 2026 legislative session, lawmakers introduced . The median bill gets only a few minutes of total debate across both chambers. said it plainly: "I know that the public wants every legislator to read and comprehend every bill, but in our 45-day session, it's not realistic." He even stood up, described a bill, and got it passed with no discussion, except he'd described the wrong bill (it was later corrected). Lobbyists likely fill that vacuum. According to , O'Leary hired Lincoln-Hill Partners to lobby for this development. # **Newark police arrest at least 20 protesters at Delaney Hall after new 9 p.m. curfew takes effect**
Police **[arrested between 20-25 demonstrators](https://substack.com/redirect/55293dba-48f8-45c2-98aa-d379318714be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Sunday night outside Newark's Delaney Hall ICE detention facility after enforcing a newly instituted 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew imposed by Mayor Ras Baraka to halt three weeks of violent rallies. Law enforcement closed off a quarter-mile stretch of Doremus Avenue and deployed riot gear as roughly 100 remaining protesters crowded the street outside the facility.
* **Officers deployed two rounds of tear gas,** corralling approximately 50 protesters and journalists before systematically detaining the remaining demonstrators and loading them into Essex County Sheriff's Department buses. The Department of Homeland Security posted footage captioned "Don't be this guy" showing officers dragging a seated protester, vowing "ZERO tolerance for rioters" on X.

# **Iran halts U.S. negotiations over Israel 's Beirut strikes, threatens to open new regional conflict fronts**
Iran has **[reportedly suspended communications with the U.S.](https://substack.com/redirect/b8c73fd8-94e5-491e-92a8-b1c1abd87ba0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** through mediators Monday in protest of Israel's strikes on Beirut, disrupting weeks of peace negotiations aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting formal talks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b8c73fd8-94e5-491e-92a8-b1c1abd87ba0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **What happened:** The IRGC-linked Tasnim News Agency stated Iran's negotiating team halted "discussions and exchanges of texts through intermediaries," citing Israeli operations violating ceasefire preconditions involving Lebanon and Gaza. Iranian officials demanded Israel immediately cease "aggressive and brutal operations" and completely withdraw from occupied Lebanese territory, warning "there will be no dialogue" until demands are satisfied.
* **Iran threatens complete Strait of Hormuz closure, activation of alternative conflict zones** : Tehran vowed to pursue total blockade of the critical shipping lane and activate additional regional flashpoints including Bab el-Mandeb Strait as retaliation against Israel and its supporters.
* **Suspension derails Trump administration 's months-long peace efforts**: The breakdown halts Trump's attempted diplomatic breakthrough on nuclear material disposal and Strait reopening after weeks of negotiations.

British Home Office **[canceled electronic travel authorizations](https://substack.com/redirect/015f66c4-985b-49a7-abc0-75f23b9ad945?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for far-left internet personality Hasan Piker and his uncle Cenk Uygur of The Young Turks, preventing them from attending SXSW London and speaking at Oxford University, determining their presence would "not be conducive to the public good."

name: Jim Jordan
subject: Direct from the White House
body:
A humbling message...

A humbling message...
| Friend,
---
I'm truly humbled and honored.
---
Direct from the White House, my friend President Trump said:
---
**" JIM JORDAN IS A VERY GOOD FRIEND, FIGHTER, AND WINNER... HE WILL _NEVER_ LET YOU DOWN"**
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkMHOnCAUhZ8GdxrgCuqCxd8aky7-pumiszQMXEcaAQPovH7jZPoA_-7mu-ee3HNun_OndpsLj5_aozKnm1OerUtoypKiLys-V1dwjUfGmVMuaypryi4Vq6wyVgKvULGup8ClaFm1Kqnp0i5dJ0DKVktrAYSUw8JaPjApsHLqcqKSMiZoL0TTLwhSGDosdwRYGGnpsVtdMDcmhozp1MWd6EKI1xRDY6KvNrWWsmcCH4RPhE8ZzZGwebqQ0F4KwqeC2td_Y7I6ED5Z7JnllA53hnhncN3BdBQ_G-137R6BwPj6TXBGuLw2Hq07PIERvXbbGxZDYPz-50f9P8ib53gkgwTG37f525uZGAqGQmD89VElZfen2zaXZUda-rg8X2HKV8s_Ff8XAAD__zA9jvI)
---
Coming from the President, those are powerful words.
---
President Trump knows _better than anyone_ the fight I'm waging to drain the swamp and put power back where it belongs - with _YOU_ , the American people.
---
Look, I know talk is cheap in politics. Anyone can make a promise. Anyone can say they'll fight.
---
**But I 've got the receipts to back it up**. I've been sued. I've been spied on. My phone records were seized. And the Left only attacks me, because I fight for YOU.
---
**I 'm working with the President - _behind the scenes and all hours of the day_ - to deliver on the agenda you voted for.**
---
And directly from the Oval Office, President Trump laid out the agenda **WE** are fighting for:
---
_**✅Grow our economy
✅Cut taxes
✅Slash burdensome regulations
✅Promote Made-In-The-USA products
✅Champion American energy dominance
✅Keep our border secure
✅Stop migrant crime
✅Defend your constitutional rights
✅Stopping the Radical Left ** _
---
And in just a few months, that same agenda will be voted on AGAIN in the midterm elections.
---
There's been a lot of doom and gloom about our odds of holding the House. But truth be told, Democrats now ONLY have a **2-POINT** advantage over us.
---
And that's not because voters suddenly approve of Radical Left ideas._It 's simply because our side isn't showing up to vote._
---
**If 2% more Republicans show up, we can EASILY erase the Democrats ' 2-point lead. This is a problem we can absolutely fix.**
---
_So, we are going zip code by zip code in our voter file to determine where we need more participation._
---
Friend, we've crunched the numbers and with our razor-thin majority now within the margin of error, YOUR voter profile in your zip code is the difference maker.
---
_That 's why I'm reaching out today to simply ask that you VERIFY your GOP voter profile to give me and President Trump the most accurate polling possible to ERASE the Democrats' 2% LEAD over us._
---
[**Please complete the brief questionnaire to verify that YOU are among the highest propensity voters we can count on in the midterms - and then I'll officially mark you as "verified" in our GOP Voter file for your zip code. **](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkMHOnCAUhZ8GdxrgCuqCxd8aky7-pumiszQMXEcaAQPovH7jZPoA_-7mu-ee3HNun_OndpsLj5_aozKnm1OerUtoypKiLys-V1dwjUfGmVMuaypryi4Vq6wyVgKvULGup8ClaFm1Kqnp0i5dJ0DKVktrAYSUw8JaPjApsHLqcqKSMiZoL0TTLwhSGDosdwRYGGnpsVtdMDcmhozp1MWd6EKI1xRDY6KvNrWWsmcCH4RPhE8ZzZGwebqQ0F4KwqeC2td_Y7I6ED5Z7JnllA53hnhncN3BdBQ_G-137R6BwPj6TXBGuLw2Hq07PIERvXbbGxZDYPz-50f9P8ib53gkgwTG37f525uZGAqGQmD89VElZfen2zaXZUda-rg8X2HKV8s_Ff8XAAD__zA9jvI)
---

[VERIFY NOW ](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkc2u2yAQhZ8G7xINYIi9YHFby1IXt6q6aJYWhiGmMmABdl6_cpQ-wN3NfHPm52jun9On9quPj586oDKHn3KZrM9oqssp1AWfi6-4pL3gxIDJC8gL0FNFG6uMlZw1qOitA86kaGmzKHQU3Nw6e-O9k3NrO5C9oQ4EWNNy2Xh1TgIJlArohLh2DrkUBno3I-eOkhb2zeqK5WpSLJgPXf2BPsZ0RileTQrNqpZat0L4B2EjYWNBs2e8Pn3MaE8FYWNFHS5_U7Y6EjZa7KhlAP1MEWfKzz4-7jVMRodN-0ckfHjdJhglTJ6VgNbvgfABg_brG1ZD-PD9z4_LfyNvXtKeDRI-_L5P397MpFgxVsKHXx-ESR3S_sqYaLKy29Ovqy_yRlp4nBte1upXX3Eo9i8AAP__KECT-A)

The partisans running the show for the last decade have underfunded public schools, endangered folks’ health care, closed rural hospitals, and watched as jobs, opportunities, and people leave Iowa to go elsewhere.

Tina Peters released from prison | | | Hi Peter, **Tina Peters walked out of prison today.** I have to admit, it hit me harder than I expected. It hit me because for a brief moment,**Colorado did something almost no other authority in America was willing to do.** Tina Peters was one of the few people involved in the Big Lie who was actually held accountable. Coloradans said there had to be consequences. A bipartisan jury in a deeply Republican county looked at the facts and reached a verdict. Coloradans stood up and said: not here. **Not our elections.** I was proud of that. But now we've opened the door. We’ve sent a signal that there **may not be consequences for tampering with elections.** We can close that door. Colorado is still a state that believes **elections belong to voters.** We are still the state that said not here. And we deserve a Secretary of State who will make sure we stay that way. Hi friend — Thank you. I want to say that before anything else. This month, people chipped in to a campaign for Lieutenant Governor of Rhode Island — an office that most Rhode Islanders couldn't fully describe if you asked them, because it hasn't given them much reason to. That's not a knock on anyone; it's just the reality of what the office has been: a title, a backup plan, a ribbon-cutting machine. And the fact that you showed up to fund the argument that it could be something different, in the middle of a political moment that is exhausting and deliberately designed to make people feel powerless, genuinely means something to me. I've been traveling across Rhode Island this month, and what I keep seeing are people who are frustrated but not checked out, who feel like their government doesn't work for them but haven't stopped believing it _could_. They show up to a house party on a Tuesday night and spend two hours asking real questions about how the LG's office works, what powers it actually has, and what it could do with the right person in it. The gap between what people think government can do and what it could actually do with the right people running it is enormous, and closing that gap starts with showing up and telling the truth about it. Your support this month funds the ability to do exactly that at scale: mailboxes, digital ads, community organizing across all 39 municipalities, events in places that haven't seen this campaign yet. The message only reaches people if we can actually get it to them, and that's what you’re making possible. If you haven't had a chance to give yet and you'd like to: [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sue_email#chip-in**](https://sue4ri.com/l/ce1jUb5DhdSP) With real gratitude, Sue _P.S. | | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEJune 1, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**LOUISIANA COTTON & GRAIN ASSOCIATION ENDORSES LETLOW FOR SENATE** _Support from Louisiana agriculture leaders highlights continued momentum behind Letlow’s U.S. Senate campaign_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed conservative candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, announced that she has earned the endorsement of the Louisiana Cotton & Grain Association.
The endorsement adds to the growing support Letlow has built across Louisiana’s agriculture community as farmers, producers, and rural leaders rally behind her campaign for the United States Senate.
_“Julia Letlow understands the challenges facing Louisiana agriculture because she has shown up, listened to our producers, and fought for our communities in Congress,”_**said Louisiana Cotton & Grain Association Executive Vice President Bobby Skeen.** _“She has been a strong advocate for Louisiana farmers, and we know she will continue fighting for our agriculture industry in the United States Senate. The Louisiana Cotton & Grain Association is proud to endorse Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate.”_
_“Louisiana’s farmers work hard every single day to feed and fuel this country, and they deserve a strong conservative voice in the Senate who will fight for them,”_**said Congresswoman Letlow.**_“I’m incredibly grateful to have the support of the Louisiana Cotton & Grain Association, and I will continue working to protect our agriculture economy, support rural communities, and stand up for the families who keep Louisiana agriculture strong.”_
As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, Letlow has worked to support Louisiana agriculture, rural infrastructure, and disaster relief for producers across the state. She has consistently championed policies that strengthen Louisiana’s farming economy and protect the future of rural communities.
Letlow advanced to the runoff in first place after a strong showing across Louisiana, winning 52 of the state’s 64 parishes. Her campaign continues to build momentum as Louisiana Republicans rally behind her campaign to send a strong conservative voice to the United States Senate.
